scope: Capture-off 1080p Metal with an offscreen presenter, whole GPU timed-pass span and named graph timestamps. Each stop has a fresh renderer and a settled cooked-valley interval. Startup work before confirmed cooked residency is labelled on each frame.
history: M1 reported a noon scene GPU pass-sum p95 change of 22.66 to 25.15 ms. See .orchestrate/evidence/v1-workload/G3S-HANDOFF.md, lines 847–877.

M2 recorded midnight 1080p scene GPU pass-sum p50/p95 of 3.94–4.39/4.52–9.17 ms with stars on and 5.76–5.89/6.81–10.59 ms with stars off, under shared load of 27.67–29.37. See .orchestrate/evidence/v1-workload/G3S-HANDOFF.md, lines 704–722.
scrub_observation: Metal T2 realtime scrub retained all 479 submitted frames in the 10 s interval. Several visible short holds appear; median submitted interval 17.820 ms and longest 86.936 ms at 4.605 s. See the retained timeline and iostat.

investigations.scrub hitch: The opportunity clock reports 119 missed starts and the writer/GPU readback rings report zero omissions. Around the capture the iostat rows show the CPU often fully busy under concurrent jobs. Before the continuous-input capture the equivalent elapsed scene held 600 submissions with a longest 27.165 ms interval under lighter load. The holds align with missed CPU-side frame opportunities, not a second encoded duplicate or missing image of a submitted frame. This is an engine capture tripwire; device cadence has its own qualification.
